text:
Maya: hey folks — first day! trying to get my onboarding PR to pass CI but both Buildkite and the GH Actions job are failing. Buildkite shows a permissions error and the GH job can't access secrets. anyone know who I should ping? :wave:

Jack: welcome Maya! :tada: most likely either the GitHub App (Buildkite) isn't installed for that repo or you don't have the right org team membership to trigger builds / read secrets. can you paste the first error?

Maya: here's the Buildkite build log snippet i see right after I push the branch:

```
Buildkite: Error: User does not have access to pipeline repository (install_buildkite_github_app: permission denied)
Exit code: 1
```

Maya: GH Actions log says:

```
Error: The workflow is not allowed to access secrets. If you recently changed repo permissions, enable the Actions permissions or add the workflow to an allowed list.
```

Tess: hm looks like two separate but related issues. steps: 1) make sure the Buildkite GitHub App is installed in the org and has access to the repo (org owners or the person who installed the app picks repos). 2) make sure you're a member of the org team that grants CI rights (we use `infra-ci` for onboarding). 3) Repo Settings -> Actions -> General -> Workflow permissions should be set to "Read and write" if the job needs to push statuses or use secrets.

Jack: @Maya do you have a link to the repo? if not, ping @tess or me and we'll check the GitHub App install page. Also, if your account is SSO-enforced you might need to reauthorize the GitHub App after SSO mapping.

Maya: repo is github.com/redwood-inference/platform-config (private). I'm in the org but not in infra-ci team yet. who can add me?

Tess: i can add you. quick checklist i'll run: grant Buildkite app access -> add Maya to infra-ci team -> enable Actions workflow permissions. should take 5–10m.

devops-bot: Build #4121 failed on "platform-config/test" — status: failed — reason: Unauthorized (pipeline: repo access)

Sam: FYI if the job also tries to push container images to ECR you'll need an IAM role scoped to ecr:PutImage & ecr:GetAuthorizationToken. common stuck point for new hires trying the docker -> ECR flow. example policy we attach to the CI role: 

```
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": ["ecr:GetAuthorizationToken","ecr:BatchCheckLayerAvailability","ecr:PutImage","ecr:InitiateLayerUpload","ecr:UploadLayerPart","ecr:CompleteLayerUpload"],
      "Resource": "*"
    }
  ]
}
```

Maya: nice catch, the job does try to push a test image. I don't have AWS creds configured locally yet so wasn't expecting that failure, good to know.

Tess: done — Buildkite app now shows installed for platform-config, and i've added you to infra-ci. i also set the repo Actions permission to Read and write. try re-running the Buildkite job or re-triggering the GH Action.

Maya: re-running now... :crossed_fingers:

devops-bot: Build #4122 started on "platform-config/test" — queued on agent group: general

Maya: looks like the Buildkite step that pulls secrets still failed with a 403 from GH Actions when trying to read ACTIONS_SECRET_TOKEN. any idea?

Jack: if you were added to the team just now, permissions sometimes take a couple minutes to propagate. also double-check the repo's environment protection rules: if the secret is tied to an environment that requires approvals, the workflow won't get it. open repo -> Settings -> Environments and see if the env is restricted.

Maya: aha environment had required reviewers set. removed the restriction and retried. build passed! :party_parrot: thanks everyone.

Tess: awesome — welcome aboard again. ping me or @jack if anything else blocks your first-week checklist. we'll do a quick CI walkthrough tomorrow. :coffee:
